paper.title: Stochastic Linear Optimization under Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear optimization under bandit feedback (compact decision set D in R^n)
unmapped: Costs need only satisfy E(c_t(x)|H_t) = mu.x for all histories (martingale-difference noise), costs in [-1,1] and mu.x in [-1,1]
Learner needs access to a barycentric spanner of D
settings.definition_quote: Let D ⊂ R^n be a compact (but otherwise arbitrary) set of decisions... Each such choice results in a cost ℓ_t = c_t(x_t) ∈ [−1, 1]. We assume that, regardless of the history H_t, the conditional expectation of c_t is a fixed linear function, i.e., for all x ∈ D, E(c_t(x) | H_t) = µ · x ∈ [−1, 1].

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear optimization, product of circles D_n = (S^1)^{n/2} (lower bound)
unmapped: Decision set is the Cartesian product of n/2 unit circles; costs in {-1,+1}; mu uniform on D_n/n
settings.definition_quote: Assume n is even. Let D_n = (S^1)^{n/2} be the Cartesian product of n/2 circles... Our cost functions take values in {−1, +1}, and for every x ∈ D_n, the expected cost is µ · x, where nµ ∈ D_n.

tuning: beta_t = max(128 n ln t ln(t^2/delta), (8/3 ln(t^2/delta))^2)

source.quote: Theorem 1(Problem Dependent Upper Bound) ... Suppose the decision set D and the true mean µ have a gap ∆ > 0. We have: • ConfidenceBall2 : For all sufficiently large T , the cumulative regret RT of ConfidenceBall2 (D,δ) is with high probability at most O(n^2/∆ log^3 T). More precisely, Prob(∀T, RT ≤ 8nβT ln(T)/∆) ≥ 1 − δ

results.notes: n = d. Regret R_T defined via means (random variable); bound holds w.p. 1-delta uniformly over T. Equivalent to O(n^2 log^3 T / Delta). Paper says results extend to time-varying decision sets (Section 7).

tuning: implemented to only choose extremal points of D

source.quote: • ConfidenceBall1 : If ConfidenceBall1 is implemented so that it only chooses extremal points xt ∈ D (which is always possible) then, for all sufficiently large T , the cumulative regret RT of ConfidenceBall1 (D,δ) is with high probability at most O(n^3/∆ log^3 T). More precisely, Prob(∀T, RT ≤ 8n^2 βT ln(T)/∆) ≥ 1 − δ

results.notes: Polynomial time given a linear optimization oracle over D (O(n) oracle calls per round).

source.quote: Theorem 2(Problem Independent Upper Bound) ... • ConfidenceBall2 : For all sufficiently large T , the cumulative regret RT of ConfidenceBall2 (D,δ) is with high probability at most O∗(n√T)... More precisely, Prob(∀T, RT ≤ sqrt(8nTβT ln T)) ≥ 1 − δ.

results.notes: O*(n sqrt T). Holds also when Delta = 0.

source.quote: • ConfidenceBall1 : For all sufficiently large T , the cumulative regret RT of ConfidenceBall1 (D,δ) is with high probability at most O∗(n^{3/2}√T)... More precisely, Prob(∀T, RT ≤ sqrt(8n^2 TβT ln T)) ≥ 1 − δ.

results.notes: O*(n^{3/2} sqrt T); efficient with linear optimization oracle.

source.quote: Theorem 3 (Lower Bound) If µ is chosen uniformly at random from the set Dn /n, and the cost for each x ∈ Dn is in {−1, +1} with mean µ · x, then, for every algorithm, for every T ≥ 1, E R = E_µ E (R | µ) ≥ (1/10) n √T. where the inner expectation is with respect to observed costs.

results.notes: Bayesian regret with uniform prior on the scaled product of circles; regret through means. Instance has Delta = 0. Since it is a Bayesian average, it also implies a minimax pseudo-regret lower bound.
